Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). 1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andesim.
2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).
8	#ifndef ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <functional>
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Free-space headroom a tier must have beyond the requested size.
18	inline constexpr long long kMmapSafetyMargin = 256LL * 1024 * 1024;
19	
20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andesim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};
26	
27	// resolve_mmap_dir result: the chosen dir ("" on failure) and, when a tier
28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).
29	struct MmapDirChoice {
30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;
32	};
33	
34	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
35	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
36	// to the argparse-style message. Fractional values truncate (1.5G -> whole
37	// bytes).
38	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
39	
40	// L26/F2: the physical shared mmap is one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES)
41	// larger than the program's --mem-size, so the V-register transport page sits
42	// just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout -- low stack, top-of-
43	// RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling -- can reach a page past its own
44	// RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. The vsim side parks the scratch
45	// at the mmap's top page (v_scratch_gpa), which equals ram_base + program_bytes.
46	long long physical_mmap_bytes(long long program_bytes);
47	
48	// The largest --mem-size whose physical mmap still fits the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM
49	// window (program_bytes + scratch page <= 2 GiB). --mem-size is capped here.
50	long long max_program_mem_bytes();
51	
52	// First-fit resolver over `tiers`. `probe(dir)` returns the dir's free bytes,
53	// or -1 when it does not exist. A tier fits when probe >= size + margin.
54	// On success `err` is empty; when nothing fits, returns {"", ""} and `err`
55	// names every tier's reason plus the HSIM_MMAP_DIR hint. Pure: no env, no
56	// filesystem -- testable with a fake probe.
57	MmapDirChoice resolve_mmap_dir(
58	    const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers, long long size,
59	    const std::function<long long(const std::string&)>& probe,
60	    std::string& err);
61	
62	// The andesim cache root: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim, else ~/.cache/andesim,
63	// else "" (no HOME). Shared by the mmap tier list and the repro bundles.
64	std::string andesim_cache_dir();
65	
66	// Build the real tier list from the environment:
67	//   HSIM_MMAP_DIR set -> that single pinned tier;
68	//   else            -> /dev/shm, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME|~/.cache + /andesim
69	//                      (created here so the free-space probe can see it).
70	std::vector<MmapTier> mmap_tiers();
71	
72	// WSL2 advice for `doctor`: given /proc/version contents, the repo dir, and
73	// the mmap tier list, return warning lines. Empty when not on WSL2. On WSL2:
74	// always the .wslconfig memory= hint (tmpfs is capped by the WSL VM), plus a
75	// drvfs warning for the repo or any tier dir under /mnt/ (slow, and
76	// MAP_SHARED is not coherent across the 9p boundary). Pure -- testable.
77	std::vector<std::string> wsl_warnings(const std::string& proc_version,
78	                                      const std::string& repo_dir,
79	                                      const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers);
80	
81	// Convert a --mem-size spec into the fast leg's plain QEMU `-m` argv:
82	// {"-m", "<MiB>M"}. Empty spec -> {} with no error (QEMU as-is). Malformed
83	// specs and sizes that are not a whole MiB (QEMU's -m granularity) return {}
84	// and set `err`.
85	std::vector<std::string> qemu_m_args(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
86	
87	// Allocate a sparse mmap file of `size` bytes in the resolved dir (mkstemp +
88	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line
89	// (plus "; fallback: <why>" when /dev/shm was skipped), and return its path.
90	// On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file (unlink when
91	// done).
92	std::string allocate(long long size, std::string& err,
93	                     const std::string& prefix = "hsim-shm.");
94	
95	}  // namespace andes_sim
96	
97	#endif  // ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
98

input.reason: Read all of driver/shm.cpp and driver/shm.hpp: no symbol from <sys/stat.h> is used (no struct stat, stat/fstat/lstat, mkdir, chmod, umask, mode_t, or S_* constants; the only grep hit, "struct statvfs", belongs to <sys/statvfs.h> on line 12). Every symbol the file does use is declared by a header that remains: statvfs (<sys/statvfs.h>), mkstemp/getenv (<cstdlib>/glibc stdlib.h), close/truncate/unlink (<unistd.h>), snprintf (<cstdio>). shm.hpp is included before line 11 and depends only on <functional>/<string>/<vector>, so no transitive reliance exists. driver/CMakeLists.txt compiles shm.cpp as a plain TU in four targets and no file #includes any .cpp, ruling out unity-build side effects. Removing the include is compile-time only; no output, exit-code, file-layout, or test-expectation change is possible (mkstemp sets mode 0600 internally, needing no S_* constants).
